contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with the packet C66-GEO-COMP demand for components, stabilizers, and finite-cover behaviour of Z, and with corroborated FND-0132 and FND-0144, which it explicitly distinguishes. INDEPENDENT CHECK. (1) Naming of H. For a connected qcqs k-scheme U and a geometric point u, pi_1^{et}(U,u) is the arithmetic fundamental group of the k-scheme U. Stacks Lemma 58.14.3 (0BTX), independently fetched, states: if U_{k-bar} is connected then there is a short exact sequence of profinite groups 1 -> pi_1(U_{k-bar}) -> pi_1(U) -> pi_1(Spec k) -> 1. The proof records that the image of pi_1(U_{k-bar}) -> pi_1(U) is normal, via the Gal(k-bar/k)-orbit argument of Lemma 58.4.5. ATT-0099's theorem_statement names H as the image of pi_1^{et}(U,u) acting by left translations on the geometric fibre of the finite etale S_6-torsor Z->U, so H=H_arith. CLM-0099-3, the summary, GAP-0099-1 and the first novelty claim label the same subgroup 'geometric monodromy'. That label is correct only when k=k-bar. Independently confirmed by reading ATT-0099. (2) Component formula over k. Stacks 03SF: finite etale U-schemes are finite continuous pi_1(U,u)-sets, and connected components correspond to orbits on the geometric fibre. For a right S_6-torsor the left pi_1-action is through rho: pi_1(U,u)->S_6, the orbits are the left cosets Hg, and there are [S_6:H] of them, each of size |H|. Stacks 0BQL: a connected finite etale cover of a normal integral scheme is itself integral normal. Stacks 033N: a locally Noetherian normal scheme is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes, so connected components are irreducible. Thus Irr(Z)=H_arith\S_6 as a statement about the k-scheme Z, exactly as the theorem_statement writes it. (3) Comparison with H_geom. Restricting rho to pi_1(U_{k-bar},u) gives H_geom=rho(pi_1^geom). Under the 0BTX hypothesis that U_{k-bar} is connected, pi_1^geom is normal in pi_1^arith, so H_geom is normal in H_arith and H_geomsubseteq H_arith, hence [S_6:H_arith]<=[S_6:H_geom]. After base change the same Galois correspondence over U_{k-bar} yields [S_6:H_geom] geometric connected (hence irreducible) components, each of degree |H_geom|. The k-component count, the common degree |H|, and the conjugacy class of the component stabilizer g^{-1}Hg therefore all change. In particular Z irreducible over k (H_arith=S_6) does not imply Z geometrically irreducible (H_geom=S_6): the standard example is H_arith=S_6 and H_geom=A_6, giving one k-component that splits into two geometric components. The quotient H_arith/H_geom is a subquotient of Gal(k^s/k), not necessarily the full Galois group. (4) Scope sharpening, not a refutation. The SES and the equality 'number of geometric components = [S_6:H_geom]' require U_{k-bar} connected. ATT-0099 assumes only that S (hence U) is normal integral finite type over a char-0 field, not geometrically integral; if the constant field of U properly extends k then U_{k-bar} is disconnected and the geometric count is the orbit count on each geometric component of U separately. The identification of the H in Irr(Z)=H\S_6 with the arithmetic image does not need geometric connectedness. (5) Campaign consequences. A monodromy computation for the balanced tetragonal family over an algebraically closed field, or a topological monodromy computation over C, computes H_geom and therefore bounds the geometric component count. It equals the k-count only if k=k-bar or if H_arith=H_geom is proved separately. Downstream citations of ATT-0099 must name which pi_1 is meant. RELATION TO THE CORPUS. Distinct from corroborated FND-0132 (the connected-to-irreducible upgrade needs normality of the base and holds even for k=k-bar; FAUD-0137's parenthetical that normality does not give geometric irreducibility is a one-line caveat, not this finding). Distinct from corroborated FND-0144 (stack inertia obstructs the scheme-theoretic [S_6:H] formula over a stack base; also visible when k=k-bar). Distinct from pending FND-0149 (unrecorded descent of ATT-0088 from algebraically closed k to general k for the P^2-bundle, smoothness and regular-immersion clauses; FND-0149 itself points at this finding for the monodromy residue). Complementary to FND-0127 (scheme-to-stack scope widening; this is the field-of-definition analogue for the monodromy group). Do not merge. Kind 'obstruction' is correct for the mislabeling of H and for any downstream use of a geometric-monodromy computation as a k-component count. Merge target: none. Promote candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source. The finding's sole reviewer_engine (claude) is in this revision's excluded_engines; this audit is the first non-excluded verification.

scope.exact_mathematical_scope: Let U be a connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over a field k, u a geometric point, and Z->U a finite etale right S_6-torsor. The group H appearing in Irr(Z)=H\S_6 as a statement about the k-scheme Z is the image H_arith of the arithmetic fundamental group pi_1^{et}(U,u)->S_6. If U is normal integral and locally Noetherian, Stacks 03SF+0BQL+033N identify connected components of Z with left H_arith-cosets, so Z has [S_6:H_arith] irreducible components, each finite etale of degree |H_arith| over U, and the S_6-stabilizer of the component Hg is g^{-1}H_arith g. If moreover U_{k-bar} is connected, Stacks 0BTX gives 1->pi_1(U_{k-bar})->pi_1(U)->pi_1(Spec k)->1, so H_geom:=image(pi_1^{et}(U_{k-bar},u)->S_6) is normal in H_arith and [S_6:H_arith]<=[S_6:H_geom]; after base change the same correspondence over U_{k-bar} yields [S_6:H_geom] geometric irreducible components of degree |H_geom|. Thus irreducibility of Z over k is strictly weaker than geometric irreducibility. Campaign instance: the ATT-0099 ordering torsor Z->U over a normal integral finite-type char-0 base.
